summary:
W1-SRVDOM review, round 1: pass. I ran every acceptance item on HEAD dee1bbe and saw each decisive line. The diff stays inside the files the spec owns: game/scripts/server/ (all new, including domain_checks.gd and the .uid files), game/tests/t_server_domain.gd, t_srvdom.gd and the report. No protected or must-not-touch file is edited, and every commit has the Co-Authored-By line. I also merged the branch into the current claude/mmo-overhaul tip (31f1498, which now includes W1-COMBAT, W1-SAVE and W1-LIGHT) in a scratch copy (git merge-tree, no conflicts) and ran t_srvdom there: '[t_srvdom] PASS', 'replay lines=3231 byte_identical=true', no SCRIPT ERROR lines.

Probes that held:
- Deposit then receive across accounts, then replay: identical.
- A captured_animal (a stack that spans several slots) through deposit and receive, then replay: identical.
- A partial deposit followed by a full deposit gives distinct uids, and both come back.
- A deposit aimed at a lock slot of a multi-slot stack is refused.
- An error injected inside a world read rolls the op back: server_error, state and journal unchanged.
- Hostile types (bool option, int node_id, float cell, count 0 or -5, duplicate picks, out-of-range slot, empty rid, NaN or Inf positions) are refused with the state unchanged and the invariants holding.

No blockers or majors. The minors are mostly post-merge drift and growth limits that W3 needs to know about.

Not checked: the accessory equip path (the data has no accessory items to test with), and power-cut durability beyond the torn-tail test.

findings.problem: W1-COMBAT, merged to claude/mmo-overhaul in 781b3b3 after this branch's last merge trial, moved the melee formula into data/combat_tuning.json, read through CombatTuning: work_tool_mult, defense_factor, min_damage_frac, crit_base, crit_per_melee_level, crit_mult and hit_reach_slack_m 0.3. It also computes hit chance as accuracy x (1 - dodge). The server keeps hard-coded copies (0.45, 0.5, 0.05, 0.08, 0.002, 1.75), uses dodge only, and uses a 0.5 m slack. The numbers match today, apart from the slack. Any edit to combat_tuning.json would make server and client diverge silently, and combat_tuning.json is not in DATA_FILES, so data_changed would not flag it either. The report's integrator hooks do not mention this.
findings.fix: Post-merge: read CombatTuning.section("player_melee") in _attack and use CombatTuning.hit_chance(base_accuracy, dodge). Add res://data/combat_tuning.json to DATA_FILES. Either use hit_reach_slack_m or keep REACH_SLACK as a stated server allowance. Record this as an integrator hook next to the rolls_burn one.

findings.problem: bool(a.get("clear", false)) runs on client-supplied JSON. act.equip {"clear": "yes"} or {"clear": {...}} raises 'SCRIPT ERROR: Invalid call. Nonexistent 'bool' constructor.' on the server; my probe hit this. The ErrorCount rollback turns it into server_error with the state unchanged, so nothing is lost. Still, any client can write script errors into server logs on demand, and the request comes back as server_error when it should be bad_request. char.move's reset has the same pattern, though only the server calls it.
findings.fix: Accept only a real bool, for example `var clear: Variant = a.get("clear", false); if not clear is bool: return no("bad_request", ...)`, and do the same for reset.

findings.problem: s.exported_assets keeps the canonical body of every asset ever deposited and never prunes it. Assets sold on the market never come back, so their entries stay forever. Each one goes into every snapshot, and _run makes a shallow copy of the whole dict on every op as the rollback backup. Per-op cost and snapshot size therefore grow with the world's lifetime deposit count, and no op exists for the economy to say a deposit was settled.
findings.fix: Record it as a W3 hook now: add a server-only op (for example char.settled {uid}) that the vault bridge calls once the ledger has taken the asset, and keep only the in-flight entries. Or back up only the keys an op touches instead of copying the dict.

findings.problem: The whole parsed args dict is journaled, unknown keys included. act.gather {node_id, option, junk: <200 KB>} succeeded in my probe and wrote a 200,253-byte journal line. The 64 KiB frame cap in contracts.md bounds this per op, but a client can still make the journal and the replay bigger with junk that does nothing.
findings.fix: Journal only the keys each op reads, for example a per-op allow-list in IntentHandlers, or cap the canonical args size and refuse anything over it with bad_request.

findings.problem: On the merged tree, act.capture succeeds only once in 10,000 ops ('act.capture':[1,310]); it was 2 on this branch. The test requires at least one success per intent, so any change to capture odds or creature tuning will turn this into a deterministic failure that says nothing about what actually broke. The report notes the risk but leaves it in.
findings.fix: Make captures likely in the fuzz: seed knocked-out, low-HP creatures and put nets in the starting fixture, or add a short scripted capture-success check and drop capture from the 'must succeed in fuzz' list.

findings.problem: domain_checks.gd is 495 lines of test code inside the runtime scripts directory, so it ships in exports (including the web build). Both t_server_domain.gd and t_srvdom.gd match W1-QA's t_*.gd glob, so the gate runs the same 6-second suite twice.
findings.fix: At integration, move domain_checks.gd under game/tests/ (or exclude game/scripts/server/domain_checks.gd from export presets) and keep one of the two runners.

findings.problem: The documented shortcut ServerRng.seed_global reseeds the process-wide RNG on every craft. On the merged tree, W1-ITEMS moved the burn roll into Crafting.rolls_burn(rec, skill, rng), so server crafts never burn until the integrator applies the hook. I confirmed that rolls_burn and build_output(..., burnt) exist at 31f1498. The hook is documented exactly in the report.
findings.fix: Integrator: apply the report's replacement line (build_output(..., Crafting.rolls_burn(rec, ch.level_of(tree), rng))) and delete seed_global as part of the merge.
